s.398(2) = proviso to old s.201(1) relief where deductee filed return and paid tax (FAQ Q6.19). Time-limit for order: s.398(5) - later of 6 years from end of tax year deductible, or 2 years from end of tax year of correction statement (Q6.18).

sections.t: Penalty equal to tax not deducted
sections.note: For pre-1.4.26 failures s.271C of old Act continues via s.536(2)(c),(d) (FAQ Q6.17). New-Act equivalent for post-1.4.26 defaults VERIFIED from bare Act: s.448 imposes penalty equal to the tax the person failed to deduct or pay or ensure payment of (incl. deemed-deduction failures under 393(3) Note 2 / 393(1) Sl.8 Note 6); s.449 is the TCS-collection mirror. Reasonable-cause defence survives via s.470 (old 273B analogue). s.447 (unrelated 172-report penalty) was omitted by FA 2026.

For pre-1.4.26 failures old s.272A(2)(g) continues (FAQ Q6.16). New-Act equivalent VERIFIED from bare Act: s.465(2)(g) imposes Rs 500/day for failure to furnish the s.395(4) TDS/TCS certificate (old s.203 analogue), capped at the tax amount by s.465(3)(b); reasonable-cause defence via s.470 (covers s.465(2)). Late TDS/TCS statements fall under s.465(2)(k)-(m) (statements u/s 397(3)).
Search initiated before 1.4.26: ALL connected proceedings (including block assessments u/s 158BC) continue under the 1961 Act (FAQ Q3.15, Q10.11).

Old-Act losses carried forward under new Act in the manner of the old Act, within original 8-year (business loss) limits; nature preserved (FAQ Q8.2-Q8.5). Belated old-Act loss returns do NOT qualify (Q8.8).
Unutilised MAT/AMT credits remain eligible under new Act; 15-year total window (FAQ Q2.25, Q2.26).
s.536(2) preserves approvals, registrations, circulars, notifications, pending applications and liabilities not inconsistent with the new Act (FAQ Q1.7, Q10.6-Q10.10).

Old regime: rebate up to Rs 12,500 where total income <= Rs 5,00,000 (unchanged in the 2025 Act). New regime (default): rebate up to Rs 60,000 where total income <= Rs 12,00,000 (raised from Rs 25,000 / Rs 7 lakh by Finance Act 2025, effective TY 2026-27), with marginal relief just above Rs 12 lakh. Rebate applies against income-tax payable before health & education cess; special-rate incomes (e.g. 111A/112A capital gains, winnings) are excluded. Resident individuals only.
